newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WAUGH AND LAW MAUL WEST INDIES ATTACK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WAUGH AND LAW MAUL WEST INDIES ATTACK.

text.p: Australian opener Mark Waugh mauled West Indies with a brilliant century to lift his side to a massive 281 for four in their limited overs World Series match on Sunday.
Number three Stuart Law followed Waugh's example only to fall seven runs short of a deserved hundred as Australia savaged an impotent West Indies bowling attack at the Gabba.
Waugh played at his stylish best to reach his ninth hundred in one-day internationals before being run out for 102 in the 40th over.
The pair added 147 runs for the second wicket in exploiting the ideal batting conditions after Australian captain Mark Taylor won the toss.
Their efforts provided Australia with an ideal platform to beat West Indies for the first time in six meetings in Brisbane over the years.
Law appeared poised to record his second limited overs century for Australia before West Indies vice-captain Brian Lara took an outstanding one-handed catch at cover point.
Waugh hit two sixes, a feat matched by Law, and five fours in a dashing, entertaining innings during which he faced 114 balls.
West Indies were handicapped by a lingering hamstring injury to fast bowler Curtly Ambrose, whose efforts in the field were badly restricted as a result.
The giant Antiguan bowled all but one of his ten-over quota but he was untypically expensive, conceding 53 runs, including five no balls, without reward.
